name: Example: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Trinomial Quadratic Factor
worked_solution:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
\mathcal{D} = 1^2 - 4(1)(1) = -3 < 0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+x+1}+\frac{C}{x-2}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x^2+x+1)(x-2)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-x & =(Ax+B)(x-2)+C({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get  $A=2,$ $B=1,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{4x^2-x}{(x^2+x+1)(x-2)} = \dfrac{2x+1}{x^2+x+1} + \dfrac{2}{x-2}.
$$

Now we integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration only at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}+\frac{2}{x-2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u = x^2+x+1.$ Then $(2x+1) \, \textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+x+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|.\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+K\end{aligned}
$$
